title: Nest after-hours tips versus the Ellington job
summary: At the Nest he made $40 or $50 in tips over his $75 pay but left for Duke, and Braud's encouragement that the band would go places kept him there.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: That's where I made more money, at the Nest, than I made on the regular job, just staying there playing for the -- big shots used to come after their show off Broadway.
Did you have a regular job in addition to the job at the Nest; at the same time?
That was the regular job but --
And then you also played there after hours?

The boss said if you wanted to make some money, you can stay there and make some money because they'd tip, you know. Helen Morgan and all those kind of people used to come there. And they'd have a ball -- sometimes I wouldn't get home till 12 at noon. But I had me about 40 or $50 in my pocket, too. And my job only paid me about 75. That's right.
And I left all that to go with Duke.
Whom I think you said was paying less

Oh, yeah. So the boss (at the Nest) said -- well, he tried to discourage me from going. Well, I said I got to try it anyway. So he said, "Well, if you're not satisfied, you're job is always waiting for you."

After I got to working in a big band, and I kind of liked it, and Braud kept telling me, "Millet, this guy's going to go places. We're going to make some money. Stay. Don't leave. Stay." And I stayed and we did make money. He told me right.
